_readme: RATCHET for scripts/pipeline/check-pr-title.mjs. A PR title's conventional-commit scope must resolve to a module, an area directory, or a named area. An entry here lets ONE scope that resolves to nothing pass anyway, so an in-flight PR whose title was written before the gate existed is not failed by it. ENTRIES MAY BE REMOVED, NEVER ADDED. A growing baseline is the gate failing open: the correct fix for a new title is to retitle the PR to the module it changes (gh pr edit <n> --title), which is what the prompt's `module:` value already tells you. Shape mirrors docs/qa/sot-refs-baseline.json and scripts/pipeline/module-baseline.json ({_readme, entries}) so there is one baseline pattern in this repo, not three. The checker matches an entry against BOTH the raw scope and its slice-suffix-normalised form, so one entry covers a whole cluster (`scopesub` covers `scopesub-s5`, `-s6`, `-s7`) rather than needing a fresh entry per slice - a per-slice baseline is a baseline designed to grow. NOT YET CI-ENFORCED: there is no check-title-baseline-ratchet.mjs and no ci.yml step comparing this file's entry set against origin/main, exactly as module-baseline.json records for itself. Until one exists, 'may only shrink' is a convention a reviewer enforces by eye. Wiring it (alongside check-sot-baseline-ratchet.mjs, which already does this for the sot baseline) is the obvious next slice. Do NOT write a count of entries into this prose: entries.length is the count. SEEDED EMPTY, DELIBERATELY, AND THIS IS A MEASUREMENT NOT AN OVERSIGHT. The gate's prompt specified six seed scopes - scope, scope-cards, scope-sub, pricing, export, crm-wincount-slice3 - measured on 2026-09-01 at origin/main b30e166a against the four PRs open that day (#1477 export, #1478 scope-sub, #1479 board, #1480 pr-prompts). RE-MEASURED 2026-09-07 at origin/main 21c98545: every one of those PRs is closed, the repo is ~280 PRs further on, and the open set is exactly two - #1758 and #1746, both feat(rates), both of which PASS on the vocabulary with no baseline at all. Seeding six dead entries would have created six burn-down obligations that never protected a single PR, and would have taught the gate to accept `export` and `pricing` forever. The scopes that DID fail in merged history (scope-card, scope-costs, scopesub, ew-2c, ew-2d, tender-lifecycle, jr-s1, tip-id-s1, station-00, 00-supervisor) are deliberately NOT seeded either: this gate runs per-PR on open PRs and never re-litigates merged history, so an entry for a merged title protects nothing - it only widens what the gate accepts next time.
